_doc: The World Government and Marine hierarchy. LADDERED: tiers and members are rung-stacks — the reader sees the hierarchy as it looked at THEIR chapter. Structure (2026-08-22 restructure per maintainer): Imu is a TIER OF ONE above the Five Elders, not their peer; the God's Knights and the World Nobles are in the chart; notes are written in the Codex's plain register. A tier's `style` picks its visual treatment. Members appear when the reader learns they BELONG here, not at debut. Maintainer QA flags in _qa_flags.
_qa_flags: Garling: appointed to the Five Elders (filling Saturn's seat) -- chapter used is 1125, QA the number and wording. Saturn deceased CONFIRMED by punk_records status.
Shamrock: punk_records has a Ch. 907 debut (Reverie cameo); his God's-Knight commander reveal is gated at 1136 -- QA that reveal chapter and the living-blade detail.
God's Knights first appearance as a unit: 1086 used; 'Holy Knights' verbal mention may be ~1083.
Nerona-D: rung stops at family name (1086); if a later chapter confirmed the D., supply chapter + wording.
Nusjuro's blade named 'Shimotsuki' -- chapter needed before it enters a rung.
Imu 1189-1191 new-form rung -- maintainer wording needed.
Approximate chapters: Tsuru 556, Kong 594, Stussy-CP0 892, Coby-SWORD 1061, Onigumo-fruit 1111.
COVERAGE PASS 2026-08-24 -- chapters below need a maintainer eye.

'Coby' renamed to 'Koby' on both cards: punk_records keys him as Koby, so character.html?name=Coby returned 'No record'. 'Coby' is kept as an alias on the record. Revert if the house form is Coby.

'Bomba (Marine)' and 'Ukkari (Character)' carry a wiki disambiguator inside the punk_records `name` field, so the chart prints it. Both are named that way deliberately: the plain forms link to the wrong record ('Bomba' resolves to chr:01687, a Tontatta of the Straw Hat Grand Fleet) or to none at all. Fix belongs in punk_records — see docs/data-integrity.md.

rungs.label: The Empty Throne
rungs.summary: Above every authority the world knows. Officially, no one sits here.

rungs.note: The Reverie revealed the throne is occupied and that the Five Elders kneel to its occupant. The world has not been told.
Hidden true ruler of the World Government. Ordered the erasure of Lulusia; spoke the name 'Lili' to King Cobra shortly before his death. Family name: Nerona.

rungs.label: The Five Elders (Gorosei)
rungs.summary: The highest publicly known authority of the World Government — above even the Fleet Admiral.

rungs.label: The Five Elders (Gorosei)
rungs.summary: The highest authority the public knows — and, as the Reverie showed, not the true apex.

rungs.note: Five unnamed elders who direct the World Government from Mariejois.

rungs.role: The highest authority known to the public
rungs.note: Five unnamed elders directing the World Government — seen at the Reverie kneeling before the Empty Throne's occupant.

rungs.role: Elder · Warrior God of Science and Defence
rungs.note: Oversaw the Egghead operation in person.

rungs.role: Elder · Warrior God of Science and Defence
rungs.note: True form: a monstrous spider-ox (ushi-oni). Led the Egghead operation in person.
True form: ushi-oni. Held responsible for the Egghead failure; his seat passed to Figarland Garling. (QA: chapter/wording)
True form: the Itsumade bird.
True form: the boar demon Fengxi.
Carries a katana.
True form: a skeletal horse-demon (bakotsu). Fights with a katana.
True form: the sandworm.
Former Supreme Commander of the God's Knights; champion of the God Valley incident. Appointed to the vacant Elder seat. (QA: chapter)

rungs.label: The God's Knights
rungs.summary: The World Nobles' own military order — knights of the Holy Land, answerable to no Marine.

rungs.note: Champion of the God Valley incident. Presides over internal justice among the World Nobles.
Elevated to the Five Elders; the Knights' command passed on. (QA: chapter)
Leads the Knights in the field during the Elbaph operation. Wields a living blade. (QA: chapter and details)
Arrow-motif Devil Fruit user; prominent in the Elbaph operation. (QA: chapter)
Elbaph operation. (QA: chapter)
Elbaph operation. (QA: chapter)

rungs.label: World Nobles (Celestial Dragons)
rungs.summary: Descendants of the world's founding royal families, resident in Mariejois. Above the law they created.

rungs.label: World Nobles (Celestial Dragons)
rungs.summary: Descendants of nineteen of the twenty founding kingdoms, resident in Mariejois since the Government's founding. Above the law they created.

rungs.note: Shot a Fish-Man at Sabaody and was answered with a fist. The incident nearly brought an Admiral down on the archipelago.
Charloss's father.
Charloss's sister.
Saved at Fish-Man Island by Otohime; returned the debt years later.
Repaid Otohime's mercy at the Reverie by shielding Shirahoshi from Charloss.
Gave up his status to live among ordinary people. The world did not forgive his family for it.
Of the Donquixote line that stayed in Mary Geoise.

rungs.role: Of the Twenty · Queen of Arabasta
rungs.note: One of the twenty kings who founded the World Government. The Nefertari line alone declined to ascend to Mary Geoise and stayed in Arabasta.

rungs.label: Government Administration
rungs.summary: The civil side of the World Government — the officials, institutions and staff that keep it running away from the fighting.

rungs.note: Carries the Government's offers of protection to island kingdoms.

rungs.label: Judicial Authority
rungs.summary: The courts that try what the Marines bring in. A Government court's verdict is final and is not appealed.

rungs.label: Judicial Authority · Enies Lobby
rungs.summary: The Government's judicial island, where the courts sit and where the sentenced are handed to the prison ship. A trial there ends one way.

rungs.note: Tries the cases the Marines bring to Headquarters.
Three men sharing one bench; the verdict is guilty either way.
A giant of Elbaph guarding the main gate, working off a bargain the Government has no intention of keeping.
A giant of Elbaph guarding the tower gate, working off the same bargain.

rungs.label: Fleet Admiral
rungs.summary: Supreme commander of the Marines. Answers to the Five Elders.

rungs.note: 'Sengoku the Buddha'. Supreme commander of the Marines through the Whitebeard era.
Hito Hito no Mi, Model: Daibutsu. Commanded the Marines at Marineford.
Stepped down after the war; serves as Inspector General.
Magu Magu no Mi (magma). Advocate of Absolute Justice; took the post after defeating Kuzan in a ten-day duel.
Fleet Admiral of Roger's era, since promoted above the Marines. (QA: chapter approximate)

rungs.label: Admirals
rungs.summary: The Marines' three strongest — the Government's greatest individual military assets.

rungs.note: Hie Hie no Mi (ice). Operates independently by preference.
Hie Hie no Mi (ice). Lost the Fleet Admiral succession duel to Sakazuki and resigned.
Hie Hie no Mi (ice). Resigned after the succession duel; has since been sighted with the Blackbeard Pirates.
Pika Pika no Mi (light).
Ordered the evacuation ship destroyed at the Ohara Buster Call.
Promoted to Fleet Admiral.
Zushi Zushi no Mi (gravity). Blind swordsman; recruited in the post-war draft.
The second post-war recruit alongside Fujitora.
Mori Mori no Mi (forest). Entered Wano unsanctioned after the raid.

rungs.label: Vice Admirals
rungs.summary: Senior Marine officers, ranked directly below the Admirals. Most command a ship and crew of their own.

rungs.label: Vice Admirals
rungs.summary: Senior Marine officers, ranked directly below the Admirals. Most carry Devil Fruits or proven Haki.

rungs.role: Vice Admiral / Hero of the Marines
rungs.note: The Marine who repeatedly cornered Roger.

rungs.role: Vice Admiral / Hero of the Marines
rungs.note: Roger's lifelong rival. Luffy's grandfather. Declined promotion to Admiral more than once.
Woshu Woshu no Mi. Strategist of Sengoku's generation. (QA: chapter approximate)
Moku Moku no Mi (smoke). Pursued the Straw Hats from Loguetown onward.
Moku Moku no Mi (smoke). Promoted after the war; commands G-5.
Commanded the escort of Boa Hancock to the war. (QA: chapter approximate)
Six-armed officer of the Marineford line.
Kumo Kumo no Mi, Model: Rosamygale Grauvogeli (ancient spider Zoan). (QA: chapter approximate)
Marineford veteran.
'Shark-Cutter' Bastille. Dressrosa field command.
Base commander of G-5.
Placed inside the Marines as a child by the Donquixote Family.
Doflamingo's inside man since childhood. Killed by Law on Punk Hazard.
Commands the SWORD unit in the Egghead era.
Refused the order to fire on Ohara and was frozen on the shore for it.
Survived the ice. Living on an island of his own with the books he carried off Ohara.
A giant. Commands from the front rank at Headquarters.
Rarely seen without a cigar.
A giant of the Marine giant squad.
A giant of the Marine giant squad.
Works undercover as a fighter under the name Maynard the Pursuer.

rungs.label: Rear Admirals & Commodores
rungs.summary: The ranks between the branch captains and the flag officers. Most base commanders and squadron leaders sit here.

rungs.note: Briefs Headquarters on bounties and the pirates behind them.

rungs.label: Cipher Pol Aigis Zero (CP0)
rungs.summary: The Government's highest intelligence and assassination unit. Operates above Marine command. White coats, masks.

rungs.note: Former CP9. Returned to service under the white mask.
Neko Neko no Mi, Model: Leopard (awakened). Led the Egghead assignment.
Ushi Ushi no Mi, Model: Giraffe. Former CP9.
Operated in the underworld as the 'Queen of the Pleasure District'. (QA: chapter approximate)
A clone of Miss Buckingham Stussy from Vegapunk's MADS era. Turned against the Government at Egghead.
Retained under CP0 after Enies Lobby.

rungs.label: Cipher Pol 9 (CP9)
rungs.summary: The Government's covert assassination unit, embedded undercover in Water 7 for five years.

rungs.label: Cipher Pol 9 (CP9)
rungs.summary: The covert unit exposed at Water 7 and Enies Lobby. Disbanded; its strongest members moved up to CP0.

rungs.note: Embedded at Galley-La as a shipwright.
Embedded at Galley-La as an inspector.
Embedded as Iceburg's secretary. Later acquired the Awa Awa no Mi.
Embedded as a Water 7 bartender. Doa Doa no Mi (door).
Inu Inu no Mi, Model: Wolf.
Iron Body specialist.
Life Return technique; prehensile hair.
Director of the Enies Lobby operation.
Newly assigned; has not completed the unit's training.
Called the Buster Call down on Ohara. Spandam's father.
Held the post before Wano; imprisoned after losing the Gomu Gomu no Mi in transit.

rungs.label: Cipher Pol (Units 1–8)
rungs.summary: The Government's eight public intelligence agencies. They gather information, and their agents are placed where information is.

rungs.note: Cooks as he fights, and calls it ramen kenpo.
Placed undercover as a nurse.

rungs.label: SWORD
rungs.summary: A covert Marine cell outside the formal chain of command. Members resign on paper and remain active.

rungs.note: Embedded inside the Beasts Pirates as a Tobi Roppo.
Rose from chore-boy to captain under Garp's training. (QA: chapter approximate)
Captured by the Blackbeard Pirates on Hachinosu; escaped during Garp's rescue assault.
Garp-trained alongside Coby.
Sniper; Egghead-era operations.
Egghead-era operations.
Vice Admiral in command of the unit.

rungs.label: Marine Branch Officers
rungs.summary: The Government's police of the four Blues — the first face of justice most islands ever see. Some wear it better than others.

rungs.label: Marine Branch Captains & Special
rungs.summary: Captains, instructors, base commanders and special-operations leads.

rungs.note: 'Axe-Hand' Morgan. Ruled Shells Town through fear and statues.
'Axe-Hand' Morgan. Arrested by his own men after the Shells Town incident.
Took command at Shells Town after Morgan's arrest. Enlisted Coby.
Enlisted at Shells Town after escaping Alvida's crew. Dreams of being an admiral.
Taken on by Vice Admiral Garp for training alongside Helmeppo.
Garp's trainee. His resolve at Water 7 impressed the wrong grandfather.
The rookie who screamed for the war to stop at Marineford — and was heard.
Morgan's son, stripped of privilege and started from the bottom.
Trains alongside Coby under Vice Admiral Garp.
Garp-trained; Coby's partner since Shells Town.
Made the mistake of criticising the Baratie's soup.
'Iron Fist' Fullbody. Demoted after Loguetown; serves under Hina.
Commands the branch nearest the Conomi Islands.
On Arlong's payroll for years — the reason no report from Conomi was ever answered.
The former Black Cat hypnotist, reformed and enlisted under Hina.
Swordswoman; catalogues named blades to recover them from criminal hands.
Smoker's second at G-5. Swordswoman and meito cataloguer.
'Black Cage' Hina. Ori Ori no Mi.
'Ship-Cutter' T-Bone. Sea-train pursuit at Water 7.
Vegapunk's bodyguard; commands the Pacifista escort.

rungs.label: Marine Officers & Base Personnel
rungs.summary: The rank and file — the officers, specialists and staff who hold the branches together.

rungs.note: Left the service and raised two girls on a mikan farm in Cocoyasi.
Attends Vice Admiral Garp and says little.
Ate the Sabi Sabi no Mi and rusts what he touches.
Placed inside the Donquixote crew under his birth name; the family knew him as Corazon.

rungs.label: Special Science Group (SSG)
rungs.summary: The Government's research arm, built around one scientist and the six satellites he made of himself.

rungs.note: The world's foremost scientist. Works for the Government from Egghead.
Handles the island's defence and its money.

rungs.label: Impel Down
rungs.summary: The Government's great undersea prison. Six levels, each worse than the one above, and officially no one has ever escaped it.

rungs.note: Ate the Doku Doku no Mi. His poison is the prison's last line.
Makes no secret of wanting the Chief Warden's post.
Oversees the demon guards of Level 4.
Commands the Blugori of Level 3.
Held the post until he was locked up for killing prisoners at his own discretion.

rungs.label: The Seven Warlords of the Sea
rungs.summary: Seven pirates the World Government has taken into its service. Their crimes go unpunished; in exchange the Government may call on them, and their existence keeps other pirates in check.

rungs.label: The Seven Warlords of the Sea (abolished)
rungs.summary: The Levely voted the system out of existence. Marine forces moved on the former Warlords the same day the decision was announced.

rungs.note: The world's greatest swordsman. Hunts pirates at his own leisure.
Rules Arabasta's underworld from Rainbase behind the face of a national hero.
Attends the Government's summons and treats them as an amusement.
Reads through every meeting and speaks only when he must.
Holds Thriller Bark in the West Blue fog and takes the shadows of those who land there.
Given the seat as payment for handing Portgas D. Ace to the Government.
Empress of Amazon Lily. Attends the Government's summons only when it suits her.
Fish-Man Island's protector. Held the seat until he gave it up rather than fight Whitebeard.
Appointed on the strength of the Impel Down escape and the crew of former inmates he came out with.
Took the seat by delivering a hundred pirate hearts to the Government.
Claims to be Edward Newgate's son and hunts down the old crew's remnants.
